headline: Volume has plateaued at ~30 km/week across eight weeks, but Tuesday's lactate threshold of 4:24/km @ 178 bpm anchors that base with a quality marker worth tracking forward.
summary:
The four-week load is essentially flat — 127 km vs 125 km prior, +2% — and the 12-week average of 29.9 km/week reflects a deliberate middle band rather than a build or a taper. With 9 runs in each of the last two four-week blocks and run frequency holding at roughly 2.2/week, this is consistent consolidation rather than drift. The 538 km year-to-date figure is substantially ahead of last year's 86 km at this point, though last year's baseline is too low to draw direct conclusions from — the more meaningful reference is your own 12-week trajectory.

Thursday's 15.73 km at 4:49/km (HR 161) remains the standout session of the recent window — a solid aerobic-threshold effort by pace and HR — and yesterday's 13.77 km at 5:48/km with HR 137 reads as a well-controlled easy follow-up the next day. That back-to-back pairing (moderate quality → easy longer run) is a durable structural pattern for ultra readiness. The lactate threshold reading from yesterday — 4:24/km @ 178 bpm — is a single data point without 30-day context yet, but as an opening baseline it sits meaningfully faster than your marathon pace and close to your 10K average pace territory, which is a reasonable threshold position for this phase of training.

Strength is at 4 sessions across the last four weeks (1 session/week), slightly below your year-to-date average of 1.3/week. No alarm there given the running load, but worth noting if the gap widens further. Your 20-week running streak has matched your personal best, which reflects consistent week-to-week execution regardless of volume fluctuation.
